title: Evidencing Reasonable Steps
summary: How senior managers create a contemporaneous record that shows they understood their area, acted on risks and escalated issues, without generating defensive paperwork.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How senior managers create a contemporaneous record that shows they understood their area, acted on risks and escalated issues, without generating defensive paperwork.
Learning Objectives: Identify the records that best evidence reasonable steps
Design a personal accountability file proportionate to the role
Use minutes, challenge and escalation records to evidence decisions
Syllabus: What good evidence looks like: contemporaneous, specific and decision-focused
Board and committee minutes as evidence of challenge
Personal accountability files, attestations and their limits
Intended Audience: Executive directors, senior managers and heads of business lines holding senior manager functions
Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit and other control functions with personal accountability
Company secretaries, HR and compliance staff who administer the accountability regime
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some management experience in a regulated firm is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
